hints.title: Ascending Array Ordering
hints.text: Sort the elements to cluster extreme values predictably.

hints.title: Greedy Triplet Partitioning
hints.text: Form each triplet by assigning one minimal value and two largest available values.

hints.title: Stride-Based Median Selection
hints.text: Accumulate elements stepping downward from the second highest element by intervals of two.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def maxMedianSum(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        n = len(nums)
        k = n // 3
        # To maximize the 2nd largest of each triplet, pick 1 smallest and 2 largest
        # Medians are picked at indices: n-2, n-4, n-6, ..., n-2k
        ans = 0
        for i in range(k):
            ans += nums[n - 2 - 2 * i]
        return ans
```

variables: N: total count of numbers in nums
complexity.notes: Sorting followed by linear stride index accumulation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all triplet permutations requires exponential combinations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting in-place uses minimal auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that pairing 1 smallest with 2 largest maximizes median yield.
